lines.text: His life is to a certain extent like the running of a race, in
which he wishes to attain his own true being.
But this is also true of him who is not strivingor not
essentially striving for any such particular goal, but who
sees the meaning of life in the education of himself, in the
formation of his own inner culture, in the perfecting of
himself and his capacities; who wishes to make something
of himself, who works at himself in order to be able to stand
the test of his own self-examination. "Before each of us there
hovers an ideal of what we must become, and so long as we
have not reached it, our hearts are restless."
Such a one too lives in the strength of the future, of what
he is not yet. He himself knows that he has not yet reached
his goal. And the more frankly he admits this to himself,
the more he becomes aware how often he has gone and goes
astray, how often he has lost himself instead of finding
himself, how often he has been guilty of falling short of his
ideals. And just as little as he would care to stand exposed
to the eyes of all in his present state, so much the more, in all
his restlessness, is he comforted by the thought that his true
being is not what he here and now is, but rather what he
hopes one day to become. Hence no doubt it is generally true
that all men live by the inspiration of the future, whether
they are clearly aware of this or not. But it makes a decisive
difference whether the future which animates and fashions the
life of a man is a real and genuine future, i.e. whether it is
only dreamed of, longed for, striven for, or whether it is in
fact coming to me. For after all, the future is what is coming
to us whether we hope for it, expect, and are prepared for it,
or not.
The extent to which men are living in view of the real
future is shown simply by this, namely, how far they are able
to deal with what the future brings to them, or whether on
the contrary they collapse and are crushed under it, be it joy
or pain or the dreary round of humdrum duties. Hence to
live in such a way as to be ready to meet the future means
to be available for whatever the future brings, in the assur-
ance and conviction that all must work together for good,
